Let $(Y,S,\mu)$ be uniformly $d$-to-one and $f:Y\rightarrow{R}$ be a tree adapted function to a compact metric space $R$ with metric $D$. The function $f$ is called \textit{generating} if the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$ is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel sets of the space $R$. Informally, ``tree very weak Bernoulli'' means that for almost all pairs of points in $Y$ their trees of preimages are close. To give a formal definition note that since $S$ is uniformly $d$-to-one, for almost all points $y\in Y$ the set $S^{-k}(y)$ contains exactly $d^k$ points, i.e. the tree of preimages is a $d$-regular rooted tree. The set $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ of finite words over $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ can be considered as a $d$-regular rooted tree, where every word $v$ is connected with $vx$ for $x\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and the root is the empty word $\emptyset$. We can use the tree $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ to label the trees of preimages. For almost all points $y\in Y$ there is a map $T_y:\{1,\dots,d\}^*\rightarrow{Y}$ such that $T_y(\emptyset)=y$ and $T_y(\sigma(v))=S(T_y(v))$ for all nonempty words $v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Every map $T_y$ is tree adapted, and it is uniquely defined up to an automorphism of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Then $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are called {\it tree very weak Bernoulli} if for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$ such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$ \begin{equation} t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon, \end{equation} where the minimum is taken over all automorphisms $\psi$ of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Notice that the definition of $t_n$ does not depend on the choice of $T_y$. Let us show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is tree very weak Bernoulli for the identity map $id:\lims\rightarrow\lims$. It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map $T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$. It is enough to show that $ t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$. Using (\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$ for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$). Thus, taking $\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that \[ t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon \] for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$. Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Hoffman-Rudolph criterion: the system is uniformly $|X|$-to-one (tree adapted factor) and, with the identity as generating function, tree very weak Bernoulli since tile diameters shrink.

nodes.name: Hoffman-Rudolph criterion (Theorem 5.5)
nodes.statement: A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$ is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli.
assumptions: A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$
conclusions: is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli.

nodes.name: Tree distance $t_n$
nodes.statement: t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon,

nodes.name: Measure $\mathsf{m}_\mathsf{e}$ on the limit solenoid
nodes.statement: In the same way we introduce the measure $\mathsf{m}_\mathsf{e}$ on the limit solenoid $\sol$ as the push-forward of the uniform Bernoulli measure on $X^{\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 23 (inverse limit)
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that $(\sol,\mathsf{e},\mathsf{m}_\mathsf{e})$ is the inverse limit of dynamical systems $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ (see \cite[page~27]{dyn_sysII}). In particular, we get
nodes.statement_short: The solenoid system is the inverse limit (natural extension) of the limit dynamical system, which is one-sided Bernoulli.

nodes.name: Solenoid system is two-sided Bernoulli
nodes.statement: $(\sol,\mathsf{e},\mathsf{m}_\mathsf{e})$ is conjugate to the two-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.
conclusions: $(\sol,\mathsf{e},\mathsf{m}_\mathsf{e})$ is conjugate to the two-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.

nodes.name: Finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group.

nodes.name: Contracting surjective virtual endomorphism with faithful action
nodes.statement: Let $\phi:H\rightarrow G$ be a contracting surjective virtual endomorphism such that the associated self-similar action is faithful (i.e. $\phi$-core($H$) is trivial in the terminology of \cite{sidki:virt_nilp}).

nodes.name: Limit $G$-space of a nilpotent group is its Malcev completion (Theorem 6.1.6)
nodes.statement: The group $G$ and its subgroup $H$ are uniform lattices of a simply connected nilpotent Lie group $L$ by Malcev's completion theorem. The isomorphism $\phi:H\rightarrow G$ extends to a contracting automorphism $\phi_L$ of the Lie group $L$. There exists a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi:\limGs\rightarrow L$ such that $\phi_L(\Phi(t))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(t)\cdot g_0)$ for every $t\in\limGs$ and fixed $x_0\in X$ and $g_0\in G$.
nodes.statement_short: $G,H$ are lattices in a nilpotent Lie group $L$, $\phi$ extends to a contracting automorphism $\phi_L$, and there is a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi$ from the limit $G$-space to $L$.
conclusions: There exists a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi:\limGs\rightarrow L$ such that $\phi_L(\Phi(t))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(t)\cdot g_0)$ for every $t\in\limGs$ and fixed $x_0\in X$ and $g_0\in G$.

nodes.name: Push-forward of $\mu$ is Haar measure
nodes.statement: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ is the (right) Haar measure on the Lie group $L$.
conclusions: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ is the (right) Haar measure on the Lie group $L$.
nodes.label: haar

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 24
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is a non-zero regular Borel measure on $L$. It is left to prove that it is translation invariant. Since the measure $\mu$ is $G$-invariant and the map $\Phi$ is $G$-equivariant, the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant. By the property of the map $\Phi$ we have $\phi_L(\Phi(A))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(A))g_0$ for every Borel set $A\subset\limGs$. Notice that since the map $\phi$ is injective, we get $\mu(A)=|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ (see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop_measure lims propert}) and hence $\Phi_*\mu(B)=|X|\Phi_*\mu(\phi_L(B))$ for every Borel set $B\subset L$. It follows that the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$-invariant. Since $\phi_L$ is contracting, the set $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$ is dense in the Lie group $L$. Hence $\Phi_*\mu$ is $L$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant and scales by $|X|$ under $\phi_L$, hence invariant under the dense set $\cup_n\phi_L^n(G)$, so translation invariant.

nodes.name: Extension to virtually nilpotent groups
nodes.statement: The same observation holds in a more general setting of finitely generated virtually nilpotent groups (or under the conditions of Theorem~6.1.6).

nodes.name: Integer expanding matrix
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ integer expanding matrix, where expanding means that every eigenvalue has modulus $>1$.

nodes.name: Digit set $D$
nodes.statement: The lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$ is invariant under $A$, and we can choose a coset transversal $D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}$ for $\mathbb{Z}^n/A(\mathbb{Z}^n)$, where $m=|det(A)|$.

nodes.name: Integral self-affine tile
nodes.statement: There exists a unique nonempty compact set $T=T(A,D)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, called (standard) \textit{integral self-affine tile}, satisfying \[ A(T)=\bigcup_{d\in D} T+d. \]

nodes.name: Basic properties of integral self-affine tiles
nodes.statement: The tile $T$ has positive Lebesgue measure, is the closure of its interior, and the union above is nonoverlapping (the sets have disjoint interiors) \cite{lag_wang:self_affine}.
conclusions: The tile $T$ has positive Lebesgue measure, is the closure of its interior, and the union above is nonoverlapping

nodes.name: Integral self-affine tiles have integer measure
nodes.statement: It is well known \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_I} that the tile $T$ has integer Lebesgue measure.
conclusions: the tile $T$ has integer Lebesgue measure

nodes.name: Computing the Lebesgue measure of an integral self-affine tile
nodes.statement: The question how to find this measure is studied in \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_I,he_hui:self_affine,deng_he:int_self_affine}, and finally answered in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til}.

nodes.name: Measure of the intersection $T\cap(T+a)$
nodes.statement: A related question how to find the measure of intersection $T\cap (T+a)$ for $a\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ is studied in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til,int_two_tiles}.

nodes.name: Self-similar action of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ associated with $(A,D)$
nodes.statement: Put $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ and let $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$ be the self-similar contracting action defined by the virtual endomorphism $A^{-1}$, the coset transversal $D$, and the trivial cocycle $C=\{1,\ldots,1\}$ (see Section~3).

nodes.name: Limit $\mathbb{Z}^n$-space is $\mathbb{R}^n$ with tile $T$
nodes.statement: The group $\mathbb{Z}^n$ is the uniform lattice in the Lie group $\mathbb{R}^n$. Hence by Theorem~6.1.6 in \cite{self_sim_groups} (see also Section~6.2 there) there exists a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi:\limGs[\mathbb{Z}^n]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n$ given by \[ \Phi(\ldots x_{i_2} x_{i_1}\cdot g)=g+A^{-1}d_{i_1}+A^{-2}d_{i_2}+\ldots \] for $i_j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $g\in\mathbb{Z}^n$. The image of the tile $\mathscr{T}$ is the self-affine tile $T$.
conclusions: The image of the tile $\mathscr{T}$ is the self-affine tile $T$.

nodes.name: Push-forward of $\mu$ is Lebesgue measure
nodes.statement: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs[\mathbb{Z}^n]$ is the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
conclusions: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs[\mathbb{Z}^n]$ is the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 25
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is the Haar measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by the above example. Since the Haar measure is unique up to multiplicative constant, we have that $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$ for some constant $c>0$ and we need to prove that $c=1$. Recall that $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer by Proposition~\ref{theor_tile_measure}, and almost every point of $\limGs$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ by Proposition~\ref{points_above}. Hence $\Phi_*\mu(T)=\Phi_*\mu(\Phi(\mathscr{T}))=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer and almost every point of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $T+g$, $g\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, with respect to the measure $\Phi_*\mu$, and thus with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. It follows that, if $\chi_{T+g}$ is the characteristic function of $T+g$, then $\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ almost everywhere with respect to both measures. Hence \[ \Phi_*\mu(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})=\int_I\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}d\lambda=\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\int_{I+g}\chi_T d\lambda=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\chi_T d\lambda=\lambda(T), \] where $I$ is the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Since $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is positive, $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$ by uniqueness of Haar measure; the multiple covering by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles and a fundamental-domain integral give $\lambda(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})$, so $c=1$.

nodes.name: Lebesgue measure of a self-affine tile is the measure number of the nucleus
nodes.statement: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ of the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$.
conclusions: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ of the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$.

nodes.name: Algorithm for the Lebesgue measure of a self-affine tile
nodes.statement: The nucleus of a contracting self-similar action can be found algorithmically using the program package \cite{AutomGrp}, and the number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ can be found using the remarks after Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr}. The measures of sets $T\cap (T+a)$ for $a\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ can be found by Remark~\ref{rem_meas_inters_tiles}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the nucleus (AutomGrp), then its measure number via the eigenvector method after Proposition 3; intersections $T\cap(T+a)$ via Remark 3.

nodes.name: Relation to the Gabardo-Yu method
nodes.statement: The methods developed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} to find the Lebesgue measure of integral self-affine tiles are related to the discussion above. Take the complete automaton \cite[page~11]{self_sim_groups} of the self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$ (it actually coincides with the graph $B(\mathbb{Z}^n)$ from \cite{canon_numsys}), revert the direction of every edge, identify edges with the same starting and end vertices labeled by $(d_1,d_2)$ with the same difference $r=d_2-d_1$, and put the new label $r$ on this edge. We get the graph $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}^n)$ constructed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} and \cite{fract_numsys}. The set $W$ constructed using $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}^n)$ \cite[page~195]{gab_yu:natur_til} is precisely the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$. Hence the theory of self-similar groups provides a nice explanation to the ideas in \cite[Section~3]{gab_yu:natur_til} and the methods developed in Sections~2,4 can be seen as its non-abelian generalization.
nodes.statement_short: Gabardo-Yu's graph is obtained from the complete automaton of the action and their set $W$ is the nucleus, so Sections 2 and 4 generalize their method.

nodes.name: Integral self-affine tiles give lattice tilings
nodes.statement: It is shown in \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_II} that integral self-affine tile $T$ gives a lattice tiling of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with some lattice $L\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$.
conclusions: integral self-affine tile $T$ gives a lattice tiling of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with some lattice $L\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$

nodes.name: Do tiles of contracting self-similar actions give tilings?
nodes.statement: An interesting open question is whether this holds for any (self-replicating) contracting self-similar action $(G,X^{*})$ (or at least for self-similar actions of torsion-free nilpotent groups), i.e. the tile $\mathscr{T}$ gives a tiling of $\limGs$ with some subgroup $H< G$.

nodes.name: Rational map of the Riemann sphere
nodes.statement: Let $f(z)\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a rational map of the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d\geq 2$.

nodes.name: Existence of the invariant measure $\mu_f$ (Freire-Lopes-Mane)
nodes.statement: It is proved in \cite{invmeas_rat} that there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$ with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$.
conclusions: there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$ with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$

nodes.name: Rational maps are Bernoulli (Heicklen-Hoffman)
nodes.statement: In \cite{rational_bernoulli}, D.~Heicklen and C.~Hoffman showed that the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift, proving the conjecture in \cite{invmeas_rat,lub:entr_ration}.
conclusions: the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift

nodes.name: Bernoulli property for sub-hyperbolic rational maps via iterated monodromy groups
nodes.statement: In the case of sub-hyperbolic rational functions this result also follows from Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} using the theory of iterated monodromy groups developed in \cite{self_sim_groups}.

nodes.name: Proof via iterated monodromy groups
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a sub-hyperbolic rational function and let $\mathcal{M}=\hat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus\overline{P}_f$, where $P_f$ is the post-critical set of $f$. Then $f$ defines a $d$-fold partial self-covering $f: f^{-1}(\mathcal{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{M}$. Take a base point $t\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $T_t$ be the tree of preimages $f^{-n}(t)$, $n\geq 0$, where every vertex $z\in f^{-n}(t)$ is connected by an edge to $f(z)\in f^{-n+1}(t)$. The fundamental group $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ acts by automorphisms on $T_t$ through the monodromy action on every level $f^{-n}(t)$. The quotient of $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ by the kernel of its action on $T_t$ is the \textit{iterated monodromy group} $IMG(f)$ of the map $f$. The group $IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group and the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\mathsf{s})$ is conjugated to $(J(f),f)$ by Theorem~6.4.4 in \cite{self_sim_groups}. Under this conjugation the measure $\mathsf{m}$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$, and we can apply Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $IMG(f)$; its limit dynamical system is conjugate to $(J(f),f)$ (Nekrashevych Thm 6.4.4) and $\mathsf{m}$ goes to $\mu_f$, so Theorem 21 applies.

nodes.name: Setup suffixes
nodes.statement: Let $w=\ldots x_2x_1\in X^{-\omega}$ and denote $w_n=x_n\ldots x_2x_1$ for $n\geq 1$. Observe, that $V(w)\subseteq V(w_n)$ and $V(w_n)\subseteq V(w_m)$ for $n\geq m$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $w$ and its finite suffixes $w_n$; note monotonicity of $V$.

nodes.name: Compactness gives intersection
nodes.statement: Take a vertex $v\in \cap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n)$. Let $P_n$ be the set of all paths $e_n\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w_n$ and ending in $v$. The set $P_n$ is a finite non-empty set for every $n$, and $e_{n-1}\ldots e_2e_1\in P_{n-1}$ for every path $e_n\ldots e_2e_1\in P_n$. Since the inverse limit of a sequence of finite non-empty sets is non-empty, there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w$ and ending in $v$. Then $v\in V(w)$ and we get \begin{equation} V(w)=\bigcap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Inverse-limit (compactness) argument gives $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$.

nodes.name: Second equality
nodes.statement: From this follows that $|V(w)|=\min\limits_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ for $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Then \[ \min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} |V(w)|=\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} \min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|=\min_{w\in X^*} |V(w)| \] and the second equality of the theorem is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce the second equality.

nodes.name: Define k and O
nodes.statement: Define the integer $k=\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} |V(w)|$ and consider the set $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)\subseteq X^{-\omega}$ of all sequences $w\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $|V(w)|=k$. Define $\mathcal{O}^*$ as the set of finite words that satisfy the same condition. We have the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Define $k$, $\mathcal{O}$ and $\mathcal{O}^*$.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 block
nodes.statement: \begin{lemma} The set $\mathcal{O}$ is open and dense in $X^{-\omega}$, and $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. For each $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there is a beginning of $w$ that belongs to $\mathcal{O}^*$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{O}=\cup_{w\in\mathcal{O}^*}X^{-\omega} w$. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that $|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in X^{-\omega}$. Hence $w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $X^{-\omega} w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus measurable. Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in X^{-\omega}$ contains the subword $u$ then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$. Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$. The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*, w'\in X^{-\omega}$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is dense in $X^{-\omega}$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Inner Lemma 1 and its proof.

nodes.name: Integrate
nodes.statement: By construction of the set $\mathcal{O}$ for every $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there exist exactly $k$ vertices $v$ such that $w\in F_v$. Let $\chi_{F_v}$ be the characteristic function of the set $F_v$. Then $\sum_{v\in V}\chi_{F_v}=k$ almost everywhere. Integrating we get $\mu_p(\Gamma)=\sum\limits_{v\in V} \mu_p(F_v)=k$.
nodes.statement_short: A.e. sequence lies in exactly $k$ sets $F_v$; integrate.

nodes.name: Openness
nodes.statement: If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that $|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in X^{-\omega}$. Hence $w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $X^{-\omega} w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus measurable.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{O}$ is a union of cylinders, hence open.

nodes.name: Claim: containing u suffices
nodes.statement: Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in X^{-\omega}$ contains the subword $u$ then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$. Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: Every sequence containing a word $u$ with $|V(u)|=k$ lies in $\mathcal{O}$.

nodes.name: Suffix case
nodes.statement: If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $u$ is a beginning of $w$.

nodes.name: Monotone under extension
nodes.statement: Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Right-resolving: appending letters does not increase $|V|$.

nodes.name: General case
nodes.statement: It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: General case $w=w'uu'$.

nodes.name: Full measure
nodes.statement: The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*, w'\in X^{-\omega}$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$.
nodes.statement_short: A.e. sequence contains $u$, so $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$.

nodes.name: Density
nodes.statement: It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is dense in $X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Density.

nodes.name: Decompose B_v
nodes.statement: By construction, for every vertex $v\in V$ we have \[ B_v=\bigsqcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} xB_u \] (here the union is disjoint because the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving).
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint decomposition $B_v=\sqcup xB_u$.

nodes.name: Right eigenvector
nodes.statement: It implies \[ \mu_p(B_v)=\sum_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} p_x\mu_p(B_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{vu}\mu_p(B_{u}). \] Thus the nonzero vector $\vec \mu_p(\mathscr{B})$ is the right eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue~$1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take measures: right eigenvector of $T_p$.

nodes.name: Left inequality
nodes.statement: Similarly, \[ F_v=\bigcup_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} F_{u}x,\ v\in V, \] and, since the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving, that implies \begin{equation*} \mu_p(F_v)\leq\sum_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} p_x\mu_p(F_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{uv}\mu_p(F_{u})\quad \Rightarrow\quad \vec \mu_p(\mathscr{F})\leq\vec \mu_p(\mathscr{F}) T_p. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Decomposition of $F_v$ gives $\vec\mu_p(\mathscr{F})\le\vec\mu_p(\mathscr{F})T_p$.

nodes.name: Perron-Frobenius
nodes.statement: The standard arguments based on the theory of nonnegative matrices (see for example \cite[proof of Theorem 4.5]{he_hui:self_affine}, \cite[p. 197]{gab_yu:natur_til}, \cite{handbook:rothblum}) end the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegative-matrix theory upgrades the inequality to equality.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Given a finite labeled graph $\Gamma=(V,E)$ the problems of finding the measures $\mu_p(B_v)$ and $\mu_p(F_v)$ are equivalent, and can be reduced to right-resolving graphs.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the general case to right-resolving graphs.

nodes.name: Obstruction
nodes.statement: The problem is that the system \[ B_v=\bigcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} xB_{u}=\bigsqcup_{x\in X}x\left(\bigcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} B_{u}\right),\ v\in V \] is not self-similar in the sense that the above expression involves not only the sets $B_v$ but also their finite unions.
nodes.statement_short: The recursion for $B_v$ involves unions of the $B_u$.

nodes.name: Subset construction
nodes.statement: Introducing additional terms to this recursion corresponding to these unions we get a system with a right-resolving graph. This procedure is similar to the construction described in the proof of Theorem~3.3.2 in \cite{IntroSymbDyn}.
nodes.statement_short: Add vertices for those unions (subset construction).

nodes.name: Contraction inequality
nodes.statement: Let us show that $\mu(A)\geq |X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ for any Borel set $A$. Consider sequences which represent points of the sets $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$: \[ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g\cdot g \ \ \Rightarrow \ \ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\tau_x(A))=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g g(x)\cdot g|_x. \] It implies \[ \mu(\tau_x(A))\leq \sum_{g\in G} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu_u (T_g)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu(A). \]
nodes.statement_short: Claim $\mu(\tau_x(A))\le\mu(A)/|X|$.

nodes.name: Preimages
nodes.statement: Consider sequences which represent points of the sets $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$: \[ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g\cdot g \ \ \Rightarrow \ \ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\tau_x(A))=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g g(x)\cdot g|_x. \]
nodes.statement_short: Describe preimages of $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$.

nodes.name: Bound
nodes.statement: It implies \[ \mu(\tau_x(A))\leq \sum_{g\in G} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu_u (T_g)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu(A). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the measure.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: By applying this inequality $n$ times we get $|X|^n\mu(\mathscr{T}_v)=|X|^n\mu(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))\leq\mu(\mathscr{T})$ for $v\in{X}^n$. Since $\mathscr{T}=\cup_{u\in X^n}\mathscr{T}_{u}$ we have that \[ \mu(\mathscr{T})\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\mu(\mathscr{T}_{u})\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu(\mathscr{T})=\mu(\mathscr{T}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate and compare with $\mathscr{T}=\cup\mathscr{T}_u$.

nodes.name: Items 1-2
nodes.statement: Hence all the above inequalities are actually equalities, $\mu(\mathscr{T})=|X|^n\mu(\mathscr{T}_{u})$ for every $u\in X^n$, and $\mu(\mathscr{T}_u\cap\mathscr{T}_{u'})=0$ for different $u,u'\in X^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Equalities give items 1 and 2.

nodes.name: Approximation bound
nodes.statement: Notice that since every Borel set $A\subset\mathscr{T}$ can be approximated by unions of tiles of the same level and using items 1 and 2 we have that if $\mu(\tau_x(A))<\varepsilon$ then $\mu(A)<\varepsilon|X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximation gives a reverse continuity bound.

nodes.name: Item 3 setup
nodes.statement: It is left to prove item 3.
nodes.statement_short: Remaining: item 3.

nodes.name: Item 3 for tiles
nodes.statement: First, let us show that the assertion holds for the tiles $\mathscr{T}_v$. Since the measure $\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}$ is concentrated on the tile $\mathscr{T}$, up to sets of measure zero the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is equal $\mathscr{T}_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$ is not $x$. Really, if $t\in\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_{ux})$ and $t\in\mathscr{T}_v$ with $v\neq u, |v|=|u|$, then $\tau_x(t)\in\mathscr{T}_{vx}\cap\mathscr{T}_{ux}$ and the measure of such points is zero. Hence \[ \mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_u)=\sum_{x\in X} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Item 3 on tiles $\mathscr{T}_v$.

nodes.name: Preimage of tile
nodes.statement: Since the measure $\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}$ is concentrated on the tile $\mathscr{T}$, up to sets of measure zero the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is equal $\mathscr{T}_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$ is not $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ up to null sets.

nodes.name: Null overlaps
nodes.statement: Really, if $t\in\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_{ux})$ and $t\in\mathscr{T}_v$ with $v\neq u, |v|=|u|$, then $\tau_x(t)\in\mathscr{T}_{vx}\cap\mathscr{T}_{ux}$ and the measure of such points is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Justify via null overlaps.

nodes.name: Tile identity
nodes.statement: Hence \[ \mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_u)=\sum_{x\in X} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Self-similarity on tiles.

nodes.name: Extend
nodes.statement: Now we can approximate any Borel set by unions of tiles and pass to the limit.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to Borel sets by approximation.

nodes.name: Preimage of tile
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} we have \[ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\mathscr{T})=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}}F_g\cdot g^{-1}, \] where the sets $F_g$ are defined using the graph $\Gamma_\mathcal{N}$ (see Section~2).
nodes.statement_short: Describe the preimage of the tile via the nucleus.

nodes.name: Integer measure
nodes.statement: Thus \[ \mu(\mathscr{T})=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(F_g)=meas(\mathcal{N}), \] which is integer by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu(\mathscr{T})=meas(\mathcal{N})$, an integer.

nodes.name: At least 1
nodes.statement: Observe that $\mu(\mathscr{T})\geq 1$ because $F_g=X^{-\omega}$ for $g=1\in\mathcal{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound 1 from the trivial state.

nodes.name: OSC case
nodes.statement: If the action satisfies the open set condition then $\mu(\mathscr{T})=meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})=1$ by Corollary~\ref{cor_meas_sum_meas}.
nodes.statement_short: OSC case: measure 1.

nodes.name: Non-OSC case
nodes.statement: Suppose now that the action does not satisfy the open set condition. Then there exists an element $h$ of the nucleus, whose all restrictions are non-trivial. Let $\mathcal{N}_1$ be the set of all restrictions of $h$, and $\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1}$ be the corresponding graph. Then by Proposition~\ref{prop cup B_v eq cup F_v} \[ \sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}_1}\mu_u(F_g)=meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1})\geq 1. \] Thus $\mu(\mathscr{T})=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(F_g)\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1})+\mu_u(F_{g=1})\geq 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-OSC case: measure at least 2.

nodes.name: Define n_x
nodes.statement: For each $x\in\limGs$ we define the number $n_x$ of such $g\in G$ that the tile $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ contains $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the covering number $n_x$.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: First we prove the inequality. Let $x\in\limGs$ be represented by the pair $w\cdot g$ from $X^{-\omega}\times G$. Then $|V(w)|\geq meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$ by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}. If $h\in V(w)$ it means that the sequence $w$ ends in $h$, which by Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} means that there is a sequence $u_h\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $w$ is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot h$. It follows that $w\cdot g$ is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot hg$. It means, in turn, that $x$ belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}\cdot hg$ for every $h\in V(w)$. It follows that $n_x\geq meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove $n_x\ge meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\limGs$ be represented by the pair $w\cdot g$ from $X^{-\omega}\times G$. Then $|V(w)|\geq meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$ by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1 gives $|V(w)|\ge meas$.

nodes.name: Tiles from vertices
nodes.statement: If $h\in V(w)$ it means that the sequence $w$ ends in $h$, which by Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} means that there is a sequence $u_h\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $w$ is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot h$. It follows that $w\cdot g$ is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot hg$. It means, in turn, that $x$ belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}\cdot hg$ for every $h\in V(w)$.
nodes.statement_short: Each $h\in V(w)$ gives a tile containing $x$.

nodes.name: Conclude bound
nodes.statement: It follows that $n_x\geq meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the inequality.

nodes.name: Identify the set
nodes.statement: Consider the set $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$ defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense} using the graph $\Gamma_\mathcal{N}$, in other words $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of all $w\in X^{-\omega}$ that end in precisely $meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$ elements of $\mathcal{N}$. By the same considerations as above we see that if $w\cdot g$ represents a point $x$ with $n_x=meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$ then $|V(w)|=meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})$, that is, $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{O}$. In other words, the set $\mathcal{O}\times G$ is closed under the asymptotic equivalence relation on $X^{-\omega}\times G$, and it is the inverse image of the set $\dot{\limGs}$ under the factor map $\pi_{\limGs[]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Points with $n_x$ minimal correspond to $\mathcal{O}\times G$.

nodes.name: Open dense
nodes.statement: Since the set $\mathcal{O}\times G$ is open and dense in $X^{-\omega}\times G$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}, the same hold for $\dot{\limGs}$ in $\limGs$.
nodes.statement_short: Openness and density via Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Null complement
nodes.statement: The complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ has measure $0$, because the complement of the set $\mathcal{O}$ has measure $0$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}.
nodes.statement_short: Null complement via Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Contradiction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Take $x\in\partial\mathscr{T}$. Suppose that $x$ is covered by exactly $k=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose a boundary point is covered by exactly $k$ tiles.

nodes.name: Neighborhood
nodes.statement: Let $U\subset\dot{\limGs}$ be the neighborhood of $x$ which intersects with finitely many tiles, say with $l\geq k$ tiles. By subtracting any tile that does not contain $x$ we may suppose that $l=k$, that is, $U$ has nonempty intersection only with those tiles that contain $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a neighborhood meeting only the $k$ tiles containing $x$.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: Now, since $x$ is in the boundary of $\mathscr{T}$, there is a point $x'$ in $U$ that is not covered by $\mathscr{T}$ (otherwise $x\in U\subset\mathscr{T}$), thus $x'$ is covered by less than $k$ tiles, contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: A nearby point is covered by fewer than $k$ tiles: contradiction.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence $\partial\mathscr{T}$ is in the complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ and has measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary lies in a null set.

nodes.name: Tile measure k
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be the nucleus and $\mathscr{T}$ be the tile of the action $(G,X^{*})$. By Theorem~\ref{theor_tile_measure} and Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer} \begin{equation} \mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})=meas(\Gamma_\mathcal{N})=\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} |V(w)|=k\in\mathbb{N}, \end{equation} where $V(w)$ is defined using the graph $\Gamma_\mathcal{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: By Theorems 11 and 1, $\mu_X(\mathscr{T})=k$.

nodes.name: Preimage sets
nodes.statement: Consider \[ \pi_Y^{-1}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\bigcup_{g\in G} T_g\cdot g\quad (\mbox{here } T_g\subseteq Y^{-\omega}), \] where $\pi_Y:Y^{-\omega}\times G\rightarrow \limGs$ is the canonical projection.
nodes.statement_short: Describe the preimage of $\alpha(\mathscr{T})$ by sets $T_g$.

nodes.name: Multiplicity at least k
nodes.statement: Take $w\in Y^{-\omega}$ and let us prove that there exist at least $k$ elements $g\in G$ such that $w\in T_g$. The tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ cover the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$, and we can find $g\in G$ such that if $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ for $y=\pi_{Y}(w\cdot g)\in\limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ then $x$ belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}$. Then $x$ is represented by the sequence $u\cdot 1$ for $u\in X^{-\omega}$. Equation~(\ref{eqn_theor_meraXY_mu tile }) implies $|V(u)|\geq k$ and so there exist $k$ elements $h_1,\ldots, h_k\in\mathcal{N}$ and sequences $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in X^{-\omega}$ such that for every $i$ there exists a left-infinite path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ which ends in $h_i$ and is labeled by $(u,u_i)$. By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} \[ x=\pi_X(u\cdot 1)=\pi_X(u_i\cdot h_i)\quad\mbox{ and }\quad x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in\mathscr{T} \] for every $i=1,\ldots, k$. Then \[ \pi_Y(w\cdot gh_i^{-1})=\pi_Y(w\cdot g)h_i^{-1}=y\cdot h_i^{-1}=\alpha(x\cdot h_i^{-1})\in\alpha(\mathscr{T}) \] and thus $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots, k$.
nodes.statement_short: Every $w$ lies in at least $k$ sets $T_g$.

nodes.name: Choose g
nodes.statement: The tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ cover the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$, and we can find $g\in G$ such that if $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ for $y=\pi_{Y}(w\cdot g)\in\limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ then $x$ belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}$. Then $x$ is represented by the sequence $u\cdot 1$ for $u\in X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $g$ with $\alpha^{-1}$ of the point in $\mathscr{T}$.

nodes.name: k paths
nodes.statement: Equation~(\ref{eqn_theor_meraXY_mu tile }) implies $|V(u)|\geq k$ and so there exist $k$ elements $h_1,\ldots, h_k\in\mathcal{N}$ and sequences $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in X^{-\omega}$ such that for every $i$ there exists a left-infinite path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ which ends in $h_i$ and is labeled by $(u,u_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Get $k$ nucleus paths.

nodes.name: Tile memberships
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} \[ x=\pi_X(u\cdot 1)=\pi_X(u_i\cdot h_i)\quad\mbox{ and }\quad x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in\mathscr{T} \] for every $i=1,\ldots, k$.
nodes.statement_short: Translate paths into tile memberships.

nodes.name: Conclude multiplicity
nodes.statement: Then \[ \pi_Y(w\cdot gh_i^{-1})=\pi_Y(w\cdot g)h_i^{-1}=y\cdot h_i^{-1}=\alpha(x\cdot h_i^{-1})\in\alpha(\mathscr{T}) \] and thus $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots, k$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: Let $\chi_{T_g}$ be the characteristic function of the set $T_g$. Then $\sum_{g\in G}\chi_{T_g}(x)\geq k$ for almost all $x$. Integrating we get $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\sum_{g\in G} \mu_u(T_g)\geq k=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get $\mu_Y(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))\ge\mu_X(\mathscr{T})$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on subtiles
nodes.statement: Let us now show that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ for any $v\in X^*$. Indeed, let $n=|v|$, then it follows from Theorem \ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} that $\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v)=\alpha(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))=\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))g$ for some word $u\in Y^n$ and $g\in G$. Thus \begin{eqnarray*} \mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))&=&\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T})))\leq\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\\ &=&\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_v). \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on subtiles.

nodes.name: Use Theorem 9
nodes.statement: Indeed, let $n=|v|$, then it follows from Theorem \ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} that $\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v)=\alpha(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))=\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))g$ for some word $u\in Y^n$ and $g\in G$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 9 maps subtiles to translated subtiles.

nodes.name: Compute
nodes.statement: Thus \begin{eqnarray*} \mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))&=&\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T})))\leq\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\\ &=&\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_v). \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the bound.

nodes.name: Absolute continuity
nodes.statement: Let us prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Indeed, let $\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)<\varepsilon$, $\pi^{-1}_{X}(A)=\cup_g T_g\cdot g$. Then $\sum_g\mu_u(T_g)<\varepsilon$. It follows that there exist $v_{i,g}\in X^*$ such that $T_g\subset\cup_iX^{-\omega} v_{i,g}$ and $\sum_{i,g}|X|^{-|v_{i,g}|}<\varepsilon$. Then $A\subset\cup_{i,g}\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}\cdot g$, and we have that $\sum_{i,g}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$. Then $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute continuity of $\mu_Y\circ\alpha$.

nodes.name: Small set
nodes.statement: Indeed, let $\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)<\varepsilon$, $\pi^{-1}_{X}(A)=\cup_g T_g\cdot g$. Then $\sum_g\mu_u(T_g)<\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Small set $A$ and its preimage.

nodes.name: Cover by tiles
nodes.statement: It follows that there exist $v_{i,g}\in X^*$ such that $T_g\subset\cup_iX^{-\omega} v_{i,g}$ and $\sum_{i,g}|X|^{-|v_{i,g}|}<\varepsilon$. Then $A\subset\cup_{i,g}\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}\cdot g$, and we have that $\sum_{i,g}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover by small tiles.

nodes.name: Conclude continuity
nodes.statement: Then $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Apply subtile bound.

nodes.name: Reduction to closed sets
nodes.statement: We will now prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Since both $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ and $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ are invariant under multiplication by $g\in G$ it suffices to prove this inequality for sets $A\subset\mathscr{T}$. Since any Borel $A$ is a union of a closed set and a set of arbitrarily small measure, it suffices to prove the inequality for closed sets, as $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ by above.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the inequality to closed subsets of $\mathscr{T}$.

nodes.name: Define A_n
nodes.statement: So let $A\subset\mathscr{T}$ be a closed set. For each $n$, let $A_n$ be the union of all tiles $\mathscr{T}_v,v\in X^n,$ that have non-empty intersection with $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $A$ by tile unions $A_n$.

nodes.name: Claim A = cap A_n
nodes.statement: Let us show that $A=\cap_n A_n$. Suppose $x\in\cap A_n$, and $x$ is not in $A$. Then for each $n$ there is $v_n\in X^n$ such that $\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$ has nonempty intersection with $A$ and $x\in\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$. It follows that $x$ has some representation $u_nv_n\in X^{-\omega}$. Since the number of such representations is finite, we may choose subsequence $n_k$ such that $v_{n_k}$ is the beginning of some word $v\in X^{-\omega}$. Since $A$ is compact it follows that $A$ has nonempty intersection with $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$, thus $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$ contains at least two points, which is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Show $A=\cap_nA_n$.

nodes.name: Assume not
nodes.statement: Suppose $x\in\cap A_n$, and $x$ is not in $A$. Then for each $n$ there is $v_n\in X^n$ such that $\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$ has nonempty intersection with $A$ and $x\in\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose $x\in\cap A_n\setminus A$.

nodes.name: Subsequence
nodes.statement: It follows that $x$ has some representation $u_nv_n\in X^{-\omega}$. Since the number of such representations is finite, we may choose subsequence $n_k$ such that $v_{n_k}$ is the beginning of some word $v\in X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Extract a convergent subsequence of representations.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: Since $A$ is compact it follows that $A$ has nonempty intersection with $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$, thus $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$ contains at least two points, which is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Shrinking tiles give a contradiction.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.statement: Since $A_n$ is the union of some tiles of level $n$, which are disjoint up to sets of measure $0$, the inequality also holds for all $A_n$. Going to the limit, we get the inequality for $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Inequality for $A_n$ and pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Symmetry
nodes.statement: By interchanging $X$ and $Y$ we get the reverse inequality, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry gives the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Auxiliary graph
nodes.statement: Construct the graph $\Gamma$ with the elements of $\mathcal{N}$ as vertices, for each edge labeled by $(x,x)$ in $\mathcal{N}$ we have the edge in $\Gamma$ with the same starting and end vertices, and labeled by $x$; and for each edge in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(x,y)$ for $x\neq y$ there is an edge in $\Gamma$ with the same starting vertex that ends in the trivial element and labeled by $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Auxiliary graph $\Gamma$ redirecting non-diagonal edges to 1.

nodes.name: Identify U
nodes.statement: Then the set $\mathcal{U}$ coincides with the set $\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$. Indeed, $h\in V_{\Gamma}(w)$ if and only if there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(w,w)$ that ends in $h$, thus $w\in\mathcal{U}$ if and only if $V_{\Gamma}(w)=\{1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{U}$ is the set of sequences ending only in vertex 1.

nodes.name: Sink component
nodes.statement: For every nontrivial element $h\in\mathcal{N}$ there exists a word $v\in X^{*}$ such that $h(v)\neq v$. It follows that there exists a path in the graph $\Gamma$ from $h$ to $1$. Hence the component $\{1\}$ is the only strongly connected component of the graph $\Gamma$ without outgoing edges.
nodes.statement_short: $\{1\}$ is the only sink component.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{cor_meas_sum_meas} the measure number of $\Gamma$ is $1$, and $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$. The first statement of the lemma now follows from Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}.
nodes.statement_short: Measure number 1, so $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$ and Lemma 1 applies.

nodes.name: Saturation
nodes.statement: Let us show that the set $\mathcal{U}$ is closed under the asymptotic equivalence relation (then the set $\mathcal{U}\times G$ is also closed). It is sufficient to show that if there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ and $u\in\mathcal{U}$ ($v\in\mathcal{U}$) then $v\in\mathcal{U}$ ($u\in\mathcal{U}$). Let the path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ end in $h$. It follows that $u$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot h$. Suppose there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(v,v)$ that ends in $g$. It follows that $v$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot g$. Thus $u$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot gh$ which is asymptotically equivalent to $u\cdot h^{-1}gh$. By definition, there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $h^{-1}gh$. Since $u\in\mathcal{U}$ we get $h^{-1}gh=1$, thus $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Saturation under asymptotic equivalence.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: It is sufficient to show that if there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ and $u\in\mathcal{U}$ ($v\in\mathcal{U}$) then $v\in\mathcal{U}$ ($u\in\mathcal{U}$).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a single nucleus path.

nodes.name: Path h
nodes.statement: Let the path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ end in $h$. It follows that $u$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot h$.
nodes.statement_short: Path for $(u,v)$ ends in $h$.

nodes.name: Path g
nodes.statement: Suppose there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(v,v)$ that ends in $g$. It follows that $v$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot g$.
nodes.statement_short: Path for $(v,v)$ ends in $g$.

nodes.name: Conjugate
nodes.statement: Thus $u$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot gh$ which is asymptotically equivalent to $u\cdot h^{-1}gh$. By definition, there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $h^{-1}gh$.
nodes.statement_short: Conjugate to a $(u,u)$ path ending in $h^{-1}gh$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $u\in\mathcal{U}$ we get $h^{-1}gh=1$, thus $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $g=1$.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Since every point of $\lims$ has at most $|X|$ preimages under $\mathsf{s}$, it is enough to show that for almost every $w\in X^{-\omega}$ the map $\pi_{\lims[]}:\sigma^{-1}(w)\rightarrow\mathsf{s}^{-1}(\pi_{\lims[]}(w))$ is one-to-one.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to injectivity of $\pi$ on $\sigma$-fibres a.e.

nodes.name: Collapse implies outside U
nodes.statement: Suppose that for some $w\in X^{-\omega}$ and $x\neq y$ in $X$ we have $\pi_{\lims[]}(wx)=\pi_{\lims[]}(wy)$. It follows that $wx,wy$ are asymptotically equivalent, thus there is a left-infinite path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(wx,wy)$. It follows that the prefix of this path labeled by $(w,w)$ must end in the nontrivial element, so $w\not\in\mathcal{U}$.
nodes.statement_short: Identified preimages force $w\notin\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\mu_u(\mathcal{U})=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1}, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{U}$ has full measure.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: By definition, the map $\rho|_{\mathscr{T}_u}:\mathscr{T}_u\rightarrow\mathsf{T}_u$ is surjective, and $\mathscr{T}_u$ is compact. Hence in order to prove that $\rho$ is a homeomorphism it is left to show that $\rho$ is injective on $\mathscr{T}_u$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to injectivity.

nodes.name: Take points
nodes.statement: Take $x,y\in\mathscr{T}_u$, and let $wu\in X^{-\omega}$ represent $x$ and $vu\in X^{-\omega}$ represent $y$. Suppose that $\rho(x)=\rho(y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take two points with the same image.

nodes.name: Injectivity
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} it means that there is a left-infinite path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(wu,vu)$. Since $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$, this path must end in $1$. It follows, that $wu$ and $vu$ represent the same point of the tile $\mathscr{T}_u$, and $x=y$.
nodes.statement_short: Nucleus path over $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ ends in 1, so $x=y$.

nodes.name: Second claim
nodes.statement: To prove the second claim, take $x\in\mathscr{T}_u\cdot g\cap\mathscr{T}_u\cdot g'$. Then $x$ is represented by two asymptotically equivalent sequences $wu\cdot g$ and $w'u\cdot g'$. It follows that there is a path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $g'g^{-1}$. Then $g=g'$ since $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness of translates.

nodes.name: Define sets
nodes.statement: Consider the sets $\tilde{\limGs}=\pi_{\limGs[]}(\mathcal{U}\times G)$ and $\tilde{\lims}=\pi_{\lims[]}(\mathcal{U})$. It follows that $\tilde{\limGs}/G=\tilde{\lims}$.
nodes.statement_short: Saturated sets from $\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: Full measure
nodes.statement: Since the set $\mathcal{U}$ has measure $1$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1}, the complements of $\mathcal{U}\times G$, of $\tilde{\limGs}$, and of $\tilde{\lims}$ have measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Complements are null by Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Properness
nodes.statement: Since the group $G$ acts properly on $\limGs$, the same holds for $\tilde{\limGs}$. It is left to prove the freeness.
nodes.statement_short: Properness inherited; freeness remains.

nodes.name: Freeness
nodes.statement: Suppose $x\cdot g=x$ for $x\in\tilde{\limGs}$ and $g\in G$. Let $u\cdot h$ be a representative of $x$ in $X^{-\omega}\times G$. It follows that $u\cdot hg$ is asymptotically equivalent to $u\cdot h$, thus there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ that ends in $h^{-1}gh$. Since $u\in\mathcal{U}$ we have $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Freeness via nucleus paths over $\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence the projection $\tilde{\limGs}\rightarrow\tilde{\lims}$ is a covering map, and the statement follows.
nodes.statement_short: Free proper action gives a covering.

nodes.name: Setup and Prop 16
nodes.statement: Consider the sets $\tilde{\lims}$ and $\tilde{\limGs}$ of full measure from the previous theorem. For every $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ we have $\mathsf{T}_u\subset\tilde{\lims}$, $\mathscr{T}_u\cdot g\subset\tilde{\limGs}$ for every $g\in G$, and $\rho^{-1}(\mathsf{T}_u)=\bigsqcup_{g\in G} \mathscr{T}_u\cdot g$ by Proposition~\ref{x_j_homeo}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the conull sets of Theorem 17; tiles over $\mathcal{U}^*$ lift disjointly (Prop 16).

nodes.name: Reduce to tiles
nodes.statement: Since $\tilde{\lims}=\cup_{u\in\mathcal{U}^*}\mathsf{T}_u$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1} it suffices to show that for any $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ the restriction of $\mu_{*}$ on $\mathsf{T}_u$ is equal to the restriction of $\mathsf{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to tiles $\mathsf{T}_u$.

nodes.name: Preimages
nodes.statement: Take a Borel set $A\subset\mathscr{T}_u$ and consider its preimage $\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}} A_g\cdot g$. Then $\pi^{-1}_{\lims[]}(\rho(A))=\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}} A_g$.
nodes.statement_short: Preimages of a Borel set $A$.

nodes.name: Disjointness
nodes.statement: Here the union is disjoint because if $w\in{A_g\cap{}A_h}$ then $w\cdot g$ and $w\cdot h$ are asymptotically equivalent to $vu$ and $v'u$ respectively, for some $v,v'\in X^{-\omega}$. It follows that $vu\cdot g^{-1}$ is equivalent to $v'u\cdot h^{-1}$. Since $u\in\mathcal{U}$, $g=h$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness.

nodes.name: Compute m
nodes.statement: Hence \[ \mathsf{m}(\rho(A))=\mu_u(\pi^{-1}_{\lims[]}(\rho(A)))=\mu_u(\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}} A_g)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(A_g). \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\mathsf{m}(\rho(A))$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: By the property of the quotient measure \[ \mu_{*}(\rho(A))=\mu(A)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(A_g)=\mathsf{m}(\rho(A)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Compare with the quotient measure.

nodes.name: Recall
nodes.statement: We will use notions and results from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. First recall that a measure preserving map with entropy $\log{d}$ is called {\it uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphism} if it is almost everywhere $d$-to-one and the conditional expectation of each preimage is $1/d$. The standard example is $(X^{-\omega},\sigma,\mu_u)$, which is uniformly $|X|$-to-one.
nodes.statement_short: Recall uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphisms.

nodes.name: Uniformly |X|-to-one
nodes.statement: Next we want to show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is also uniformly $|X|$-to-one. By Proposition~\ref{prop_measure_prop_lims} the map $\pi:X^{-\omega}\rightarrow\lims$ is injective on the preimages $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for almost all $w\in X^{-\omega}$, that is, $\pi$ is {\it tree adapted} in terminology of \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. We can apply Lemma~2.3 from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}, which says that a tree adapted factor of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is again uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism. In particular, the shift $\mathsf{s}$ is the map of maximal entropy $\log |X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Show the system is uniformly $|X|$-to-one.

nodes.name: Tree adapted
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop_measure_prop_lims} the map $\pi:X^{-\omega}\rightarrow\lims$ is injective on the preimages $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for almost all $w\in X^{-\omega}$, that is, $\pi$ is {\it tree adapted} in terminology of \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}.
nodes.statement_short: Prop 15: $\pi$ is tree adapted.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: We can apply Lemma~2.3 from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}, which says that a tree adapted factor of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is again uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Hoffman-Rudolph Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Entropy
nodes.statement: In particular, the shift $\mathsf{s}$ is the map of maximal entropy $\log |X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximal entropy.

nodes.name: Quote criterion
nodes.statement: To prove the theorem, we use the following Theorem~5.5 in \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. \begin{theor} A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$ is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli. \end{theor}
nodes.statement_short: Quote Hoffman-Rudolph Theorem 5.5.

nodes.name: Recall generating
nodes.statement: Recall the definition of tree very weak Bernoulli and generating function. Let $(Y,S,\mu)$ be uniformly $d$-to-one and $f:Y\rightarrow{R}$ be a tree adapted function to a compact metric space $R$ with metric $D$. The function $f$ is called \textit{generating} if the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$ is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel sets of the space $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall generating functions.

nodes.name: Recall TVWB
nodes.statement: Informally, ``tree very weak Bernoulli'' means that for almost all pairs of points in $Y$ their trees of preimages are close. To give a formal definition note that since $S$ is uniformly $d$-to-one, for almost all points $y\in Y$ the set $S^{-k}(y)$ contains exactly $d^k$ points, i.e. the tree of preimages is a $d$-regular rooted tree. The set $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ of finite words over $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ can be considered as a $d$-regular rooted tree, where every word $v$ is connected with $vx$ for $x\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and the root is the empty word $\emptyset$. We can use the tree $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ to label the trees of preimages. For almost all points $y\in Y$ there is a map $T_y:\{1,\dots,d\}^*\rightarrow{Y}$ such that $T_y(\emptyset)=y$ and $T_y(\sigma(v))=S(T_y(v))$ for all nonempty words $v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Every map $T_y$ is tree adapted, and it is uniquely defined up to an automorphism of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Then $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are called {\it tree very weak Bernoulli} if for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$ such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$ \begin{equation} t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon, \end{equation} where the minimum is taken over all automorphisms $\psi$ of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Notice that the definition of $t_n$ does not depend on the choice of $T_y$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall tree very weak Bernoulli.

nodes.name: Verify TVWB
nodes.statement: Let us show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is tree very weak Bernoulli for the identity map $id:\lims\rightarrow\lims$. It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map $T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$. It is enough to show that $ t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$. Using (\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$ for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$). Thus, taking $\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that \[ t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon \] for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$. Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Identity is a TVWB generating function.

nodes.name: Tree maps
nodes.statement: It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map $T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$. It is enough to show that $ t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$; reduce to $t_n\to0$.

nodes.name: Small tiles
nodes.statement: Using (\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$ for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$).
nodes.statement_short: Small tile diameters beyond level $n_1$.

nodes.name: Bound t_n
nodes.statement: Thus, taking $\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that \[ t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon \] for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $t_n<\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude via Theorem 22.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is a non-zero regular Borel measure on $L$. It is left to prove that it is translation invariant.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to translation invariance.

nodes.name: G-invariance
nodes.statement: Since the measure $\mu$ is $G$-invariant and the map $\Phi$ is $G$-equivariant, the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: $G$-invariance.

nodes.name: Scaling
nodes.statement: By the property of the map $\Phi$ we have $\phi_L(\Phi(A))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(A))g_0$ for every Borel set $A\subset\limGs$. Notice that since the map $\phi$ is injective, we get $\mu(A)=|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ (see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop_measure lims propert}) and hence $\Phi_*\mu(B)=|X|\Phi_*\mu(\phi_L(B))$ for every Borel set $B\subset L$.
nodes.statement_short: Scaling under $\phi_L$ from Prop 10.

nodes.name: Density
nodes.statement: It follows that the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$-invariant. Since $\phi_L$ is contracting, the set $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$ is dense in the Lie group $L$. Hence $\Phi_*\mu$ is $L$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: Invariance under a dense subgroup gives $L$-invariance.

nodes.name: Haar
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is the Haar measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by the above example. Since the Haar measure is unique up to multiplicative constant, we have that $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$ for some constant $c>0$ and we need to prove that $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Haar uniqueness: $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$.

nodes.name: Recall
nodes.statement: Recall that $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer by Proposition~\ref{theor_tile_measure}, and almost every point of $\limGs$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ by Proposition~\ref{points_above}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall integrality and multiple covering.

nodes.name: Covering count
nodes.statement: Hence $\Phi_*\mu(T)=\Phi_*\mu(\Phi(\mathscr{T}))=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer and almost every point of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $T+g$, $g\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, with respect to the measure $\Phi_*\mu$, and thus with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. It follows that, if $\chi_{T+g}$ is the characteristic function of $T+g$, then $\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ almost everywhere with respect to both measures.
nodes.statement_short: The tiles $T+g$ cover a.e. point $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ times.

nodes.name: Integrate
nodes.statement: Hence \[ \Phi_*\mu(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})=\int_I\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}d\lambda=\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\int_{I+g}\chi_T d\lambda=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\chi_T d\lambda=\lambda(T), \] where $I$ is the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over the unit cube to get $\lambda(T)$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is positive, $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $c=1$.

nodes.name: Define IMG
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a sub-hyperbolic rational function and let $\mathcal{M}=\hat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus\overline{P}_f$, where $P_f$ is the post-critical set of $f$. Then $f$ defines a $d$-fold partial self-covering $f: f^{-1}(\mathcal{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{M}$. Take a base point $t\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $T_t$ be the tree of preimages $f^{-n}(t)$, $n\geq 0$, where every vertex $z\in f^{-n}(t)$ is connected by an edge to $f(z)\in f^{-n+1}(t)$. The fundamental group $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ acts by automorphisms on $T_t$ through the monodromy action on every level $f^{-n}(t)$. The quotient of $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ by the kernel of its action on $T_t$ is the \textit{iterated monodromy group} $IMG(f)$ of the map $f$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $IMG(f)$ via the monodromy action on the preimage tree.

nodes.name: Nekrashevych 6.4.4
nodes.statement: The group $IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group and the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\mathsf{s})$ is conjugated to $(J(f),f)$ by Theorem~6.4.4 in \cite{self_sim_groups}.
nodes.statement_short: Limit dynamical system is conjugate to $(J(f),f)$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 21
nodes.statement: Under this conjugation the measure $\mathsf{m}$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$, and we can apply Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathsf{m}$ maps to $\mu_f$; apply Theorem 21.

nodes.name: Solve eigen-system
nodes.statement: Indeed, a left eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue $1$ is uniquely defined if we know its entries $\mu_p(B_v)$ for vertices $v$ in the strongly connected components of $\Gamma$ without outgoing edges.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the eigenvector equation given the sink-component values.

nodes.name: Boundary values
nodes.statement: For every such a component $\Gamma'$, we have $B_v=X^\omega$ and $\mu_p(B_v)=1$ for every vertex $v\in\Gamma'$ if the component $\Gamma'$ is a strictly right-resolving graph, and $\mu_p(B_v)=0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary values 1 or 0 on sink components.

nodes.name: Product graph
nodes.statement: Construct a new graph $\mathscr{G}$ with the set of vertices $V\times V$ and put an edge from $(v,u)$ to $(v',u')$ labeled by $x\in X$ for every edges $v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v'$ and $u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u'$ in the graph $\Gamma$ (label products of graphs by Definition~3.4.8 in \cite{IntroSymbDyn}).
nodes.statement_short: Build the label product graph on $V\times V$.

nodes.name: Read off intersection
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that then $B_{(v,u)}=B_v\cap B_u$ (see Proposition~3.4.10 in \cite{IntroSymbDyn}).
nodes.statement_short: Read off $B_v\cap B_u$ as $B_{(v,u)}$ in the product graph.

nodes.name: Compute nucleus
nodes.statement: The nucleus of a contracting self-similar action can be found algorithmically using the program package \cite{AutomGrp}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the nucleus with AutomGrp.

nodes.name: Measure number
nodes.statement: the number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ can be found using the remarks after Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr}
nodes.statement_short: Measure number via the eigenvector method.

nodes.name: Intersections
nodes.statement: The measures of sets $T\cap (T+a)$ for $a\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ can be found by Remark~\ref{rem_meas_inters_tiles}.
nodes.statement_short: Intersections via Remark 3.
